title: Ground every lesson or label it portable; never fabricate an incident
summary: The central honesty rule from the sibling spheres: an entry is included because it is grounded in a real incident or contract, never 'because this seems like it could confuse an LLM'. If a sphere is grounded, each article cites the real file/contract/incident. If it is portable (a language best-practice used across checkouts), say that plainly with a reference label, and do not dress it up as an incident that never happened.
evidence_note: oorexx-llm-pitfalls records two invariants: nothing is on the strength of 'this might confuse an LLM', and a rule needs a real mechanical trigger while an intent-dependent trap is an article. python-best-practices labelled its items PLABEL: canonical/reference because Python is portable rather than one project's incidents.
invariants: A grounded sphere: each article states the exact file/contract/incident it came from.
A portable sphere: mark the entry reference/canonical and do not invent project incidents to make it look grounded.
Quote verifiable evidence (a file, a contract line, a changelog entry) where you can; never fabricate a quote.
Line numbers in a grounded piece are observation anchors, not gospel; point at the file and let the reader confirm.
